Minimum-of-k Likelihood-Ratio Test for an Indirect Effect (MBCO)

Source: R/sem-mbco.R
mbco_sem.Rd

Tests the null hypothesis that an indirect effect, the product of two or more labeled paths (\(a b\), or a serial \(a d b\)), is zero in a model fitted by fit_sem(). The product is zero exactly when one factor is, so the model is refitted once per path with that path set to zero; each is a linear equality constraint, so each refit is a single solve. The statistic is the smallest of the likelihood-ratio statistics, referred to a chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom (the minimum-of-k LRTs; see the Methods and Formulas article). The nonlinear constraint \(a b = 0\) is never solved, because a nonlinear solver can stop at the branch with the larger statistic.

Usage

mbco_sem(
  object,
  a,
  b,
  n_starts = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  fit = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  paths = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A SEMFit from fit_sem(), fitted without weights.

a, b

Character strings: the labels of the two free regression paths whose product is the indirect effect (for example "a" and "b" in "M ~ a*X" and "Y ~ b*M"). They must be different, and each must be a labeled ~ row of the fit; a variance, a loading, an unlabeled path and a defined parameter are refused. For a product of more than two paths pass them all as paths, or as a character vector in a with b missing.

n_starts, control

Passed to the optimizer for the two refits, as in fit_sem(). NULL, the default, uses the settings object was made with, so a better optimum in the full fit than in a refit cannot inflate the statistic; an explicit value overrides them.

fit

Renamed object; the old name still works with a warning.

paths

Character vector of two or more labels: the paths whose product is the indirect effect (c("a", "d", "b")). NULL, the default, uses a and b.

Value

An object of class c("mbco_sem", "htest"): statistic (the smallest diffLL), parameter (df = 1), p.value, method, data.name, n_obs, unresolved (TRUE when any refit failed, see Details), and tests, a data frame with one row per refit (constraint, the minimized discrepancy f, diff_ll equal to n_obs * (f - fit@f), converged, and note, the failure text of a refit that could not be fitted, otherwise empty). It prints with the standard htest layout.

Details

A fit made with weights is refused: the weighted discrepancy is not a likelihood, so its difference is not chi-square. So is a fit that did not converge, since its discrepancy is the reference both refits are measured against.

A refit that fails the acceptance gate of the optimizer does not stop the function: its row has converged = FALSE, f and diff_ll NA and the failure text in note, a warning repeats the text, and statistic and p.value are NA (never the minimum over the refits that worked, which would hide the failure). A zero-product branch that cannot be fitted stops fit_sem() itself (there is no partial fit to test against).

Inequality constraints in the model matter only when they put the null on the boundary of the parameter space. If a bound or an inequality that involves the tested parameter is active at its refit (a > 0 with the null a = 0), the function warns that the statistic is a mixture of chi-squares, not chi-square(1), and that the p-value is not valid. A bound the null sits inside (a < 0.2), an inactive inequality and one on another parameter are not mentioned. A null the constraints rule out (a > 0.3 with the null a = 0) is an unresolved row whose note says so.

Only a product of labeled paths is tested; a sum of products (several parallel indirect effects together) is not. If two of the paths are tied by an equality (a == b), their refits impose the same restriction and their diff_ll values coincide. The test is conservative: under a null where only one factor is zero its size is at most the nominal level, and with more than one zero factor it is smaller still.

See also

fit_sem(), SEMFit

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment",
  data = mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL
)
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")
#> 
#> 	Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect
#> 
#> data:  a * b = 0
#> MBCO = 17.557, df = 1, p-value = 2.788e-05
#> 

# a serial indirect effect, the product of three paths
serial <- fit_sem(
  paste0("mediator1 ~ a*treatment\nmediator2 ~ d*mediator1 + treatment\n",
         "outcome ~ b*mediator2 + treatment"),
  data = mediation_demo
)
mbco_sem(serial, paths = c("a", "d", "b"))
#> 
#> 	Minimum-of-3 likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect
#> 
#> data:  a * d * b = 0
#> MBCO = 17.557, df = 1, p-value = 2.788e-05
#> 
# }
